newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares slip slightly in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares slip slightly in early trade.

text.p: Singapore shares slipped slightly early on Wednesday as the market digested the good and bad news of the recent batch of annual results, dealers said.
"It's not all over yet and we're watching for anything that's an extraordinary or out of our expectations," said one dealer.
At 0225 GMT the key Straits Times Industrials Index had eased slightly, down 5.70 points at 2,189.05, but the market was seen to be on an upward rather than downward trend.
"Generally the market should be OK and possibly uplifted by the recent numbers and those left to come," said a local dealer.
Interest was targeted at Keppel Corp which led gainers in the early minutes of trading, rising in response to news of a one-for-four bonus issue revealed on Tuesday evening.
Its shipyard unit, Keppel FELS, continued the drop begun on Monday evening when the firm announced a weak outlook for 1997.
Meanwhile, much of the Singapore $0.50 gain made by Fraser & Neave on Tuesday was lost in the first 85 minutes of Wednesday as it led 101 losers down S$0.30 at S$13.00.
Central Properties was topping 106 gainers, up S$0.60 at S$17.50, reflecting dealers' favouritism for property stocks.
